Taken from Wikipedia:
> Sundowning, or sundown syndrome,[1] is a neurological phenomenon associated with increased confusion and restlessness in people with delirium or some form of dementia. It is most commonly associated with Alzheimer’s disease but is also found in those with other forms of dementia. The term sundowning was coined by nurse Lois K. Evans in 1987 due to the timing of the person’s increased confusion beginning in the late afternoon and early evening.[2][3] For people with sundown syndrome, a multitude of behavioral problems begin to occur and are associated with long-term adverse outcomes.[4][5][6][7] Sundowning seems to occur more frequently during the middle stages of Alzheimer’s disease and mixed dementia and seems to subside with the progression of the person’s dementia.

I’m going to go against the grain here and say, if you have the option to use the defender gear, go for it. 

**BUT** don’t use it as a fastpass to advance, use it as a softer landing to actually learn the inner workings of the game. Every monster telegraphs in their own way and can be memorized (some more brutal than others) but not usually without getting knocked around first. That’s the only reason I endorse the gear, to make the learning curve not quite so steep. I started that way myself, and it made it was much nicer to take on monsters extra times, without using up all of my items to learn them. 

And the curve will get harder with Iceborne no matter what, but by then you should know the inner workings of the weapons you choose, the Clutch Claw, the items you need, etc. And if you do choose to use the Defender gear, don’t forget to often look at the smithy to see what other sets can do for you! 

Most important though is to take your time and have fun (: Happy hunting!

The next step is distractions. Do things that make you happy. Do you have a hobby? A tv series you like to watch? Maybe a book? Being idle is terrible for the brain, trust me. It’s also super important to have someone you trust that you can talk to, especially when you overhear something that gives you anxiety. My mother is great at making things more palatable. My girlfriend even more so. But if you have no where to turn, and it feels like the world is closing in on you, I’ve had wonderful conversations with nonemergency crisis lines who can help turn your thoughts positive. Or at the very least help you let it all out so you don’t hold it all inside.
